content.title: Noah Wyle shares thrilling update on The Pitt season 3 amid HBO Max launch
content.text: The Pitt star Noah Wyle has shared exciting details about the HBO medical drama's third season, including hints it could run "forever"Lucas Hill-Paul Content Editor11:56, 26 Mar 2026Noah Wyle, star of The Pitt, has shared an exciting update on the third season of HBO's hugely popular medical drama. He also hinted at his aspirations for the future of the drama, suggesting it could continue "forever" if audiences keep tuning in.Article continues belowWyle plays Dr Michael 'Robby' Robinavitch, a senior attending physician working in a bustling and underfunded emergency room in Pittsburgh. Throughout each season, Dr Robby, along with a team of doctors, nurses, and medical students, navigate a single 15-hour shift, with the second series taking place during a busy 4th of July.‌The former ER actor was in London this week for the UK launch of the series where he revealed two crucial rules that every episode of the hit series must adhere to, reports the Mirror.‌READ MORE: The Pitt's Noah Wyle shares two strict rules every episode must followREAD MORE: Harry Potter told he's 'nothing special' in huge trailer for new TV series amid earlier release dateSpeaking to HBO Max Chairman Casey Bloys, Wyle was asked when the cast and crew will be ready to commence production on season three. "Very soon, boss, very soon," Wyle quipped. "We are in the process of writing character arcs for season three for everybody."He proceeded to explain how the series' unique storytelling format presents an intriguing challenge for the writers, which includes himself and creator R. Scott Gemmill.‌We use your sign-up to provide content in ways you've consented to and improve our understanding of you. This may include adverts from us and third parties based on our knowledge of you. More info"It's a very interesting show to break because, unlike a lot of shows that are 22 episodes that may play over a calendar year, this is 15 hours of one day," he continued. "So you're painting with a much finer brush. The character's arc is not really enough to go through the courtship of a romance, but it's enough to get your head turned."It's maybe enough to lose faith, maybe enough to find faith, but these are really small arcs that happen over the course of the day but can be really satisfying if you're engaged with that character."Article continues belowFortunately, The Pitt rapidly attracted a dedicated audience in the States, with the second series premiere drawing an impressive 7.2 million US viewers within its first week of broadcast. "We have these characters who seem to be resonating on a one-to-one with audiences," Wyle added."Everyone's feeling, 'I'm a little Javadi (played by Shabana Azeez), I'm a little Samira (Supriya Ganesh), and I have a little Langdon (Patrick Ball) in me, or I know a Whitaker (Gerran Howell)', and that makes it really exciting to see where they're going to go next, and to write for where they're going to go next."‌Teasing the third series' narrative, Bloys and Wyle disclosed that the forthcoming instalment is also building towards an explosive and potentially life-altering event in much the same manner as the first two series."We've built a pressure cooker where every hour we turn up the temperature, we add more ingredients, then just when it's about to explode we drop a piano on it," Wyle revealed. "You've done that successfully for season two and now you're thinking about it for season three?" Bloys clarified, and Wyle confirmed "Yes".Get HBO Max free with SkyThis article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn moreSky is giving away free subscriptions to HBO Max with its £22 Ultimate TV bundle, which also includes Netflix, Disney+, discovery+, Hayu, and around 135 channels at no extra cost.Article continues below"One of the gratifying things about season two is that we realised we don't need a big 'deus ex machina' plot device to keep this engaging," he said. "There's something really satisfying about watching everyday people trying to get through the course of the day, beset by all the trials and tribulations that come over the course of that day."If that is satisfying television then this show could run forever, because we don't need a helicopter to come down in the ambulance bay, we don't need to jump the shark."The Pitt is available to stream on HBO Max with new episodes on Thursdays.
